biography: Henrique Assunção, born under the relentless sun of São Paulo, Brazil, carries the fire of his homeland in every race. His journey began not on a meticulously prepared track, but on the chaotic, pothole-ridden streets of his neighborhood, where he honed his skills dodging buses and weaving through traffic on a beat-up go-kart gifted by his mechanic father. This baptism by fire instilled in him a fearlessness that borders on recklessness, a trait that both thrills and frustrates team strategists. His breakthrough came at the Brazilian National Karting Championship, where, despite starting last after a mechanical failure in qualifying, he clawed his way to victory with a daring last-lap overtake that became an instant legend. Now, at 29, Assunção is at the peak of his abilities, driving for FTR Motorsport, hungry for championships and eager to prove that his raw talent can be refined into consistent dominance. He's a constant threat on the track, and a captivating personality off it.
drivingStyle: Assunção's driving style is a blend of Brazilian flair and controlled aggression. He's known for late braking and daring overtaking maneuvers, often pushing his car and tires to their absolute limit. He attacks every corner as if it were his last, favoring a high-risk, high-reward approach. While this can lead to spectacular results, it also occasionally results in costly mistakes. Tire management is an area where he is constantly working to improve, as his aggressive style tends to punish the rubber. Under pressure, Assunção thrives, often finding an extra gear when the stakes are highest.

rivalries.name: Marco Bellini
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their karting days, fueled by a clash of personalities and several on-track collisions.

rivalries.name: Anya Volkov
rivalries.reason: A more recent rivalry, sparked by a controversial incident at the Monaco Grand Prix where Assunção's aggressive defense forced Volkov into the barriers.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: A battle of contrasting styles, with Tanaka's methodical precision clashing with Assunção's impulsive flair. Their races are often tactical chess matches fought at breakneck speed.

quirks: Always wears the same faded bracelet given to him by his grandmother before every race.
Listens to the same classic samba song before getting into the car, a ritual to connect with his roots.
Refuses to walk under ladders, a superstition he picked up from his father.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I'm here to win, even if I have to break a few rules to do it."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian Grand Prix in 2028, a home victory that cemented his status as a national hero, after battling through the field from tenth on the grid.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2027 Monaco Grand Prix, a mistake that cost him a potential championship victory.
